newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt fund managers bullish Sept 23 week - MCM.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt fund managers bullish Sept 23 week - MCM.

text.p: Anticipating an eventual slowdown in the U.S. economy, fixed-income managers remained bullish on U.S. debt over the past week, according to an MCM MoneyWatch Inc survey.
"Buyside managers are holding to a macro-view that the economy will be slowing," said MCM money market analyst Peter McTeague, who conducts the asset allocation survey.
The weekly survey showed durations as a percentage of benchmark dipped to 105.8 percent in the week ended September 23 from 106.5 percent in the prior week.

A duration reading above 100 percent indicates the group of investors polled is mostly long on the market. A portfolio's duration represents its average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
In the "next likely move" category, portfolio managers representing 23 percent of total assets in the survey said they would "buy," up from 15 percent the prior week.
Strategists leaning toward "sell" fell to 12 percent, down from 24 percent in the week ended September 16.
Sixty-five percent of managers said they were "neutral" on the market, up from 61 percent a week ago.
Cash as a percentage of assets fell to 2.66 percent, against 2.79 percent registered the previous week.

The survey showed 19 percent of investors polled overweighted the 10-plus years duration sector, down from 25 percent in the previous week, while 28 percent underweighted it. The remaining 53 percent were "neutral."
In the five- to 10-year duration sector, 40 percent of investors polled said they overweighted the securities and 23 percent underweighted them.

Asked in advance to project the outcome of Tuesday's Federal Reserve policy meeting, 62 percent of respondents said the Fed would leave interest rates unchanged. In the previous week's survey, 87 percent had called for no rate shift.
Seventy-five percent of money managers in the latest survey said the Fed will either remain on hold or make one rate hike in 1996.
The survey included 38 domestic participants, who manage about $90.0 billion in fixed-income assets. The poll is conducted weekly by MCM and usually is released on Tuesday.
